_comment: The cement and CCS census: one outside list, every entry in exactly one class.
python3 sources/build_cement_ccs_benchmark.py     # the tables, and the gate
THE LIST. The IEA CCUS Projects Database, 2026 edition — "IEA CCUS Projects
Database 2026.xlsx", updated 27/03/2026, project announcements as of February
2026. 1110 project rows worldwide; the census is of the 425 the publisher's own
`Region` column calls Europe. THE SUBSET IS THE PUBLISHER'S AND NOT THIS
REGISTER'S: no judgement of ours picks the 425, which is the only reason a gap
table over them is allowed to claim it sums to the list.
The file is held by hash and not by copy — sources/benchmark_snapshots.json,
`iea_ccus_projects_database`, where the IEA's two statements about its own
licence are recorded rather than reconciled. Entries are keyed by the IEA's own
`ID`, which is what the brief means by the benchmark's own identifier.
THERE IS NO SECOND LIST FOR THIS SECTOR AND NO DRIFT TABLE. Both absences are
findings, and each has a reason that is not the same as the other's:
CO2RE, the Global CCS Institute's facilities database, is the second list the
brief names, and it is DROPPED — not deferred. Its facilities table is a Power
BI publish-to-web embed with export disabled. Read in a browser by George
Christopoulos on 14 September 2026 (Region EUROPE, Location All, Facility
Status All) it renders rows a person can read, and it never states how many
rows Europe has. A gap table is gated on summing to the list's own entry count,
and an embed that shows rows without ever stating their number cannot supply
one. That is the refusal class: READABLE, NOT ENUMERABLE.
DRIFT IS NOT MEASURABLE FOR THIS SECTOR. Drift needs two vintages and this
register has one. The IEA product page's Schedule tab records past releases —
April 2025, March 2024, March 2023 — and its Data sets tab offers exactly one
file, the 2026 edition; no past-edition URL exists in the page. This is a fact
about what this register holds, NOT a finding about the list.
CLASSES, AND THE GATE. Each of the 425 ends in exactly one class and the counts
must sum to 425 or this script exits non-zero.
THE OUT-OF-PERIMETER CLASSES ARE DERIVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. An entry whose
sector the perimeter does not hold is refused on the publisher's own `Subsector`
value, mechanically, in `perimeter_clause()` below — 243 entries. Hand-listing
them would have invited a typo to become a class. The clause NAMES THE INDUSTRY,
per sources/scope.md "Sector perimeters": those entries are read later for the
supplier nodes and a refusal recording only "out of perimeter" throws away the
one fact that makes the later read possible.
THE IN-PERIMETER ENTRIES ARE WORKED BY HAND, one at a time, in
sources/cement_ccs_entries.json — 42 cement and 140 CO2 transport and storage.
Each carries its class, the sources read, and for an admission the capacity AT
THE UNIT THE COMPANY STATED.
NO CAPACITY COMES OFF THIS LIST. The IEA publishes two capacity columns and one
of them, "Estimated capacity by IEA", is the IEA's own computation from plant
details through the conversion factors on the workbook's Definitions tab. The
brief says no capacity conversion, capacity at the unit stated, so neither IEA
column is ever written onto a row: an admitted row takes the figure its owner
states or it carries none. Where the list's figure and the company's differ, both
are recorded as a disagreement and neither is reconciled.

entries.name: Beli Net Zero (Beli Izvor plant)
entries.failed_leg: a route stated, not a project
entries.speaker: Holcim Bulgaria, own carbon-neutrality page

entries.why: The page names the Beli Izvor works and names CCS as the route to net zero for it. It states no project, no capacity, no date and no decision, and the IEA entry carries no capacity, no FID and no operation year either. A stated route is not a company-confirmed capture project.

disagreements.held: A BOUND AGAINST A POINT VALUE, and they are not the same kind of statement. The owner states a lower bound; the list states a number that satisfies it. The row carries the bound as the owner made it.

disagreements.held: NOT A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT A NUMBER BUT ABOUT WHICH SUBSTANCE IS BEING COUNTED -- tonnes of cement against tonnes of CO2. Recorded here so a reader comparing the two does not read one as the other.

reference_debts.believed: capture at one works, Vicat's Montalieu-Vercieu cement plant, admitted once as vaia-montalieu-vercieu
reference_debts.missing: No source read says whether HyNoVi is a phase of VAIA, its predecessor, or a separate unit. Vicat's 2021 release has HyNoVi capturing 40 per cent of the works' CO2 with a 330 MW electrolyser into methanol; its 2025 release has VAIA capturing 1.2 Mt, nearly 100 per cent, into sequestration. Both are Vicat and both are Montalieu-Vercieu, and the company never states the relation.
reference_debts.needed: A Vicat page or permit naming both project names, or naming HyNoVi as superseded.

pair: IEA 202, 'Heidelberg Materials LEILAC 2' - a cement plant at Hanover, owner HeidelbergCement
IEA 556, 'Hover cement works Hannover phase 2' - a cement works at Hoever, owner Holcim Deutschland
reference_debts.believed: NOTHING IS BELIEVED HERE, WHICH IS THE POINT
reference_debts.missing: Two entries name a cement works at Hanover under two different owners. HeidelbergCement's 2021 release says LEILAC 2 was decided for 'the HeidelbergCement cement plant in Hanover'; Holcim Deutschland's 2026 release puts its test plant at 'Zementwerk Hoever, Niedersachsen'. Hoever is in the Hanover region. Either these are two works, or one of the two statements is about a works its speaker no longer owns, or LEILAC 2 moved. NO SOURCE READ HERE SETTLES IT, so the two entries are kept apart and neither is merged into the other.
reference_debts.needed: A source naming the operator of the Hoever works and the site of LEILAC 2 together, or a permit for either.

pair: IEA 539, 'Carbon Clean CEMEX Rudersdorf plant phase 1'
reference_debts.believed: two capture projects at one works, CEMEX's Ruedersdorf plant
reference_debts.missing: Both are CEMEX at Ruedersdorf and they are different technologies at different scales with different partners -- Carbon Clean's CycloneCC at 100 t/day, Linde's at 1.3 Mt/yr. Whether the first is a stage of the second or a separate installation is not stated by anyone read. 540 is admitted; 539 is held for ruling and is not merged into it.
reference_debts.needed: A CEMEX statement relating the two.

pair: IEA 1459, 'ECCO2-LH (Lighthouse) LafargeHolcim Carboneras cement factory phase 2'
reference_debts.believed: two entries at one works, Holcim Espana's Carboneras plant
reference_debts.missing: ECCO2-LH is a 2020 CCU pilot the IEA carries as Cancelled; CO2nscious is a 2025 capture entry the IEA carries as Planned. Whether the second replaces the first is stated nowhere read. Neither is admitted, so no row turns on it, and the pair is recorded so a later pass does not merge them on the shared works name.
reference_debts.needed: A Holcim Espana statement naming both.
